ordinary|for your goal, i’d use a mix of one gui regex tool, one terminal upgrade, and one browser-based drill site. **best setup** 1. **regexr**: [regexr.com](https://regexr.com/) best interactive regex playground. it highlights matches live, explains tokens, has a cheat sheet, and lets you test examples quickly. use this for regex concepts. 2. **regexone**: [regexone.com](https://regexone.com/) best beginner lesson path. short exercises, good sequencing. 3. **try ripgrep in y minutes**: [codapi.org/try/ripgrep](https://codapi.org/try/ripgrep/) browser-based interactive `rg` tutorial. good bridge from regex theory to real cli searching. 4. **iterm2** on macos better terminal than default terminal.app. use it for daily shell practice. 5. **fzf** this is the big one for interactive cli learning. it gives fuzzy search for files, history, commands, and `rg` results. the official fzf docs have a good `rg` integration walkthrough: [junegunn.github.io/fzf/tips/ripgrep-integration](https://junegunn.github.io/fzf/tips/ripgrep-integration/). install the practical tools with homebrew: ```bash brew install ripgrep fd fzf bat eza tree jq ``` then enable fzf shell integration: ```bash $(brew --prefix)/opt/fzf/install ``` useful tools: - `rg`: search file contents - `fd`: nicer `find` - `fzf`: interactive fuzzy picker - `bat`: nicer `cat` with highlighting - `eza`: nicer `ls` - `tree`: directory structure - `jq`: json querying for reverse search specifically, learn both: ```text ctrl-r ``` and fzf-enhanced history search. after installing fzf, `ctrl-r` usually becomes a much better interactive history picker. for native macos regex apps, you can try: - **patterns**: polished regex tester for macos - **expressions**: lightweight macos regex app - **regex forge**: native macos regex editor, paid/trial-style app based on current listings - **regex - learning** on the app store: structured regex lessons and live tester my recommendation: don’t over-invest in a paid regex app yet. use **regexr + regexone + your local `.tmp/cli-regex-lab` + iterm2/fzf/rg**. that will teach the actual workflow faster than a standalone app.
